question: A 50-year-old woman from a rural area presents with a fetid nasal odour that she herself cannot perceive, progressive difficulty breathing through her nose despite visibly wide nasal passages on anterior rhinoscopy, and green-black crusts. Which statement best explains the apparent paradox of nasal obstruction in a wide nasal cavity?

answers.text: The wide cavity represents post-surgical over-resection; the sensation of blockage is due to scar tissue at the nasal vestibule.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Although turbinate over-resection (empty nose syndrome) is a secondary cause of atrophic rhinitis, the classic primary ozaena presentation does not involve vestibular scarring. The paradox is physiological, not anatomical obstruction.

answers.text: Atrophy of the turbinate mucosa eliminates the normal turbulent airflow and mucosal airflow sensation, producing a subjective sense of blockage despite an anatomically wide cavity.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Normal nasal airflow sensation depends on tactile and temperature stimulation of the turbinate mucosa. In atrophic rhinitis, mucosal and turbinate atrophy eliminates this sensory input — the airstream passes freely through a wide, featureless cavity but the patient perceives obstruction. This is the paradox of atrophic rhinitis.

answers.text: The green-black crusts physically obstruct the wide cavity, explaining the sensation of blockage.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partially relevant but not the full explanation. While thick crusts do cause some mechanical obstruction, the subjective sense of nasal blockage in atrophic rhinitis is also present when the cavity is free of crusts. The primary mechanism is loss of mucosal airflow sensory perception.

answers.text: Ozaena is caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, whose biofilm reduces mucociliary clearance and causes obstruction.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The classic bacterium associated with ozaena is Klebsiella ozaenae (formerly Perococcus foetidus / Coccobacillus foetidus ozaenae), not Pseudomonas. The odour is caused by bacterial fatty acid metabolism on atrophic mucosa and crusts.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the atrophic rhinitis section. The key concept is the physiological role of turbinate mucosa in generating the subjective sensation of nasal airflow.
Correct. The paradox of atrophic rhinitis: wide cavity + subjective obstruction = loss of mucosal airflow sensation due to turbinate and mucosal atrophy.
